Both handbooks present the two as successive stages of one history: R/T p.53 write PNWGmc *awj > PWGmc *[aw'w'] > pre-OE *[auj], and Campbell §120.2 p.46 writes the ordered chain 'auj > auuj > auj'. The direction is therefore historical, not merely executable. The West Germanic intermediate is independently attested in the continental cognates (OHG houwi, gistrouwen; OS hoi). Before the 2026 repair CAPR had no rule creating this geminate and fed hay with it lexically; see sc010-w-gemination-and-hay-depth-adjudication.md.

edges.notes: Feeding. The historical direction comes from the sources, not from the displacement probe: R/T p.172 say *au was 'first tensed and fronted to æu ... later the offglide was unrounded and lowered', and the second step operates on a segment the first creates. The intermediate itself has documentary support: Fulk 2018 §4.12 p.73 says the fronting produced ēa 'at first a diphthong with a rounded off-glide, as shown by early spellings, e.g. (aeodbald) (i.e. Eadbald, name) in Bede, with rounding persisting in late Northumbrian'. The no-output set produced by displacing SC030 after SC032 must NOT be read as historical evidence. It arises because *aeu has no surface realization in the model: with SC032 first there is nothing for it to consume, and the *aeu that SC030 then creates survives to the surface and is rejected. The probe demonstrates that *aeu is a non-surface intermediate of CAPR's own; the historical interval is established by R/T p.172 and the early spellings reported by Fulk. See sc029-sc030-awj-resolution-and-au-fronting-adjudication.md §8.
